title: Density changes Tech View row, avatar and progress bar sizes as designed
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and See financial data, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
  • The design pictures DC-06-tech-view-compact-light-1440.png, DC-06-tech-view-regular-light-1440.png and DC-06-tech-view-comfortable-light-1440.png are open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); they are attached to this case.
  • In the design pictures the names, numbers, dates and amounts are sample data, and the rank numbers (1, 2, 3 …) beside rows and cards are left out of this release, so do not compare those.
  • The Comfortable design picture adds the hours under each progress bar (for example 0.8 / 8.0 hrs); the PRD says density never changes the values shown, so do not expect the hours there.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC19 Zoe Density) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC19 Abe Density) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC19 Density Sizes") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17852) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has one approved line, {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service"), whose technician is {Technician-B}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter, Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Tech View in the display switcher.
  2. Click the density button and choose Compact.
  3. Look at the rows, the group headers, the avatars and the progress bars, and compare them with the Compact design picture.
  4. Click the density button and choose Regular.
  5. Look at them again and compare them with the Regular design picture.
  6. Click the density button and choose Comfortable.
  7. Look at them again and compare them with the Comfortable design picture.
  8. Click Board View in the display switcher and click the density button.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: the rows are at their lowest (36 px in the design), the avatars are smaller and the progress bars shorter and thinner (48 × 4 px in the design), as in the Compact picture. The row text is the same size as at Regular or a little smaller (13 px in the design); write down which.
  • Step 5: the rows are taller (48 px in the design) and the progress bars 64 × 6 px, as in the Regular picture.
  • Step 7: the rows are the tallest (64 px in the design) and the avatars larger, as in the Comfortable picture.
  • Steps 3, 5 and 7: the same columns and the same values show at every density.
  • Step 8: Comfortable is the density in use in Board View too.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10049 (Story 6, Density); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S6-R1, S6-R2, S6-R3, S6-R4 and S6-R6, read 14 Oct 2026; Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html", states core__work-orders__tech-compact__light__1440, core__work-orders__tech-regular__light__1440 and core__work-orders__tech-comfortable__light__1440 (design pictures DC-06-tech-view-compact-light-1440.png, DC-06-tech-view-regular-light-1440.png, DC-06-tech-view-comfortable-light-1440.png, rendered from that export at the width in the name), read 14 Oct 2026. Covers the design defects SV-11318 (reported 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward). Where the PRD says nothing about the look, the design is the source. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

The design's Compact row text is 13 px; whether that meets the app's minimum body text size is open with the product owner (question W-11, not yet answered), so step 3 records the size without failing on it. The design adds the hours under the bar only at Comfortable; this case follows the PRD, which says density never changes what is shown (question PQ-V07, not yet answered).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-R1: “Offer Compact, Regular, and Comfortable density in Tech View and Board View.”
  • S6-R2: “Density adjusts spacing and the size of rows, cards, and their elements.”
  • S6-R3: “Share one density selection between Tech View and Board View.”
  • S6-R4: “Compact density must not reduce text below the application’s minimum body text size.”
  • S6-R6: “Changing density never changes which fields, columns, or values are displayed.”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View row height by density: “rowH: rowDensity === "large" ? "64px" : rowDensity === "small" ? "36px" : "48px"”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View text size by density: “cellFs: rowDensity === "small" ? "13px" : "14px"”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View avatar size by density: “crewSize: rowDensity === "large" ? 32 : rowDensity === "small" ? 20 : 24”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View progress bar by density: “barW: rowDensity === "small" ? "48px" : "64px"”
